transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-01-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Mark (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood SE), Jonah (CSM), Sanjay (Veridian Head of ML), Maya (Eng Mgr), Priya (InfoSec), Alex (SRE)

Summary:
Quick scoping for a 6-week pilot focused on quality eval + regression sprint. Cover success criteria (latency, cost, hallucination), workload sizing, benchmarks, timelines for golden prompts and regression tests. Next steps to exchange artifacts and schedule security deep dive.

Topics covered:
- Success criteria and acceptance gates
- Workload profile and sizing (qps, token distribution)
- Benchmark harness and metrics to collect
- Golden prompts, regression test design, hallucination/format checks
- Scoring approach: mix of automated and human review
- Timeline and ownership for pilot run

Transcript body:
[00:00] Mark (Redwood): alright everyone good to go, thanks for joining. we'll keep this short, scope the pilot and nail down who will do what. um lena, you'll lead the quality plan portion?
[00:12] Lena (Redwood): yep i'll walk through the eval outline, then we can get to the traffic numbers. hi sanjay, maya, priya, alex.
[00:20] Sanjay (Veridian): hey thanks, appreciate it. we've been chatting internally, main ask is: can this keep our control plane on-prem while using Redwood's hosted runtime for bursts? security is big.
[00:33] Priya (Veridian): yea SOC two compliance, SSO via our IDP, and bring-your-own-KMS for keys. also need audit logs per request.
[00:42] Mark (Redwood): totally, we support SAML SSO and BYOK integrations; audit logs and request-level tracing are part of Redwood Console. we'll put the SOC2 packet in the share.
[00:51] Maya (Veridian): operationally, our SREs care about p95 latency and tail behavior. if we hit bursty traffic from edge robots, we need fallback to a cheaper model without breaking format.
[01:05] Lena (Redwood): great, those are exactly the tradeoffs we want to capture in success criteria. i'll start with baseline success gates — technical and quality.

[01:18] Lena (Redwood): Success criteria proposal: 1) latency: p95 generation latency under 300ms for typical prompts at 512 token context, 2) hallucination rate below 2% on golden set (definition below), 3) format/structure pass rate 99% (JSON schema conformance on structured outputs), 4) throughput: sustained 40 QPS with 20% headroom, and 5) cost per 1k tokens improvement compared to current in-house serving.
[01:40] Maya (Veridian): can we relax p95 for bursts? our load has periodic spikes.
[01:46] Lena (Redwood): yes — we'll measure nominal and burst separately. nominal target 40 QPS p95 <300ms, burst up to 120 QPS with elastic fallback options; tail latency during bursts can be covered by model variant routing.

[02:05] Alex (Veridian): what's model variant routing? like auto-fall back to quantized smaller model?
[02:10] Jonah (Redwood): exactly, we can route to a compatible quantized variant in the same family — slightly cheaper, lower memory — automated policy. we'll test that in the benchmark.

[02:22] Sanjay (Veridian): on hallucination, how do you define it? we need reproducible checks.
[02:28] Lena (Redwood): good point. our approach: golden prompts are pairs of input + expected output constraints. hallucination is any assertion in model output that contradicts a verifiable fact in the ground truth or introduces fabricated entities. we'll use a mix of exact-match checks for structured fields and semantic checks for free text.

[02:45] Lena (Redwood): Regression + quality plan outline:
- Golden prompts: Veridian supplies 500 canonical prompts that represent the most critical flows (lab reports, robot telemetry summaries, instructions). Redwood will add 200 adversarial cases.
- Automated checks: schema conformance, numeric range checks, citation checks where applicable, and embedding-based semantic similarity against ground truth.
- Human review: a small panel (Veridian SMEs) will rate 10% sample of outputs for precision, relevance, and hallucination severity on a 5-point scale.
- Acceptance gate: pass rates as noted earlier (hallucination <2% measured on combined auto+human set).

[03:30] Maya (Veridian): 500 golden prompts sounds like a lot, but okay. is there a template?
[03:34] Lena (Redwood): yes we'll provide CSV template with fields: id, prompt_text, expected_structure (JSON schema or regex), ground_truth_answer(optional), priority flag. we'll upload it with examples.

[03:45] Mark (Redwood): also important: regression cadence. we'll run nightly regression harness during the pilot and report daily dashboards. major regressions (score drop >5% on golden set) trigger rollback or canary.

[03:59] Sanjay (Veridian): what's your scoring approach? simple accuracy? f1? matt's team uses BLEU for summarization but that misses hallucination.
[04:10] Lena (Redwood): we use composite scoring: structure_score (JSON pass/fail weighted), semantic_similarity (embedding cosine mapped to 0-100), hallucination_penalty (binary flags per case), and human_quality_score. final quality_score = 0.4*human + 0.3*semantic + 0.2*structure - 0.1*hallucination_penalty. thresholds tuned with Veridian's golden set.

[04:35] Alex (Veridian): embedding similarity — do you use sentence-transformers?
[04:38] Lena (Redwood): we use an embedding model validated for semantic similarity; we can switch to your internal embeddings if you prefer.

[04:45] Priya (Veridian): on security — do you keep any PII? how's data handled for hosted runs?
[04:51] Mark (Redwood): for pilot we'll do private deployment into a VPC peered with your network or dedicated pools depending on commitments. BYOK means keys stay with you. For hosted bursts we have contractual data handling clauses; we'll provide the DPA and SOC2 artifact.

[05:12] Sanjay (Veridian): timeline — we were thinking 6 weeks: week one onboarding and golden prompt collection, weeks two-three benchmarks and tuning, weeks four-five regression sprint, week six acceptance and wrap. is that reasonable?
[05:25] Mark (Redwood): yes very doable. quick mapping: 
- Week0 (pre-kick): exchange security docs and traffic profile
- Week1: onboarding + golden prompt ingestion + harness set up
- Week2-3: baseline benchmarking (latency/throughput) + model variant runs + initial tuning
- Week4-5: regression sprint (nightly runs, human review sampling)
- Week6: acceptance tests, final report, and recommendations.

[05:52] Maya (Veridian): what does the benchmark harness collect?
[05:55] Lena (Redwood): latency percentiles (p50,p90,p95,p99), token throughput, token-level cost, model switch events, failure/error rates, output size distribution, and per-case schema pass/fail. We'll also capture traces for slow calls (kv cache hit/miss, scheduling latency).

[06:17] Sanjay (Veridian): we'll need the JMeter script or runner to be able to replay real request sizes — our avg request is 180 tokens, p95 720, with bursts in morning ops.
[06:28] Alex (Veridian): plus some requests include attachments (small binary) that we pre-process; for those we want consistent input sizes.

[06:37] Lena (Redwood): ok we'll provide a runner that supports variable token sizes and can replay payloads from a CSV with timestamp offsets to simulate bursts. also supports canary routing to smaller model.

[06:50] Jonah (Redwood): question on acceptance — do you want cost reduction quantified? some customers want a strict cost per 1k tokens target.
[06:56] Sanjay (Veridian): yes cost target matters. our current in-house average is $0.30 per 1k tokens for generation. we'd hope for 20% improvement at least with Redwood batching and quantization.
[07:08] Lena (Redwood): we can include cost per token and per-response metrics; we'll run budgeted simulations and provide estimated savings under different batch sizes/latency SLOs.

[07:18] Priya (Veridian): audit and retention — we need logs retained for 90 days and ability to export in CSV. also need request-level redaction for PII.
[07:27] Mark (Redwood): retention policy configurable; redaction hooks can run before logs persist. we'll add that as a requirement in the security doc.

[07:36] Maya (Veridian): on model versions, we want pinning for reproducibility. how do you handle rollouts?
[07:41] Lena (Redwood): rollouts via canary with traffic split and automatic rollback on quality regressions. we store model version hashes and seed state so runs are reproducible in the harness.

[07:54] Sanjay (Veridian): ok sounds good. can you also test for hallucination around date/time-sensitive facts? our robots log timestamps and we don't want the model to invent events.
[08:03] Lena (Redwood): yes we'll craft golden prompts that check temporal consistency; automated checks can verify timestamps, and human reviewers will flag ambiguous cases.

[08:16] Alex (Veridian): curious — how do you measure hallucination rate automatically? is it reliable?
[08:21] Lena (Redwood): automated detection uses a combination: 1) structured field exact-match checks; 2) entity cross-checking against known ground truth lists; and 3) semantic divergence from ground truth answer via embeddings with thresholds tuned on validation set. we expect some false positives, which is why human sampling is part of the pipeline to calibrate thresholds.

[08:44] Maya (Veridian): what about regression case design? do you recommend mutation-based adversarial cases?
[08:49] Lena (Redwood): yes — we'll create adversarial permutations (e.g., partial context, noisy telemetry, injection attempts) and edge cases (very long context, nested JSON). Redwood will add ~200 adversarial cases; Veridian provides the canonical operational set.

[09:05] Sanjay (Veridian): scoring weight question — why give human 40%? that feels high and could bias acceptance to human reviewers.
[09:13] Lena (Redwood): we weight human review higher for precision because automated metrics don't fully capture nuance, especially hallucination severity. we can adjust weights; suggested starting point is human-heavy but we can move to 25-30% if you prefer.

[09:30] Mark (Redwood): acceptable — we'll make weights configurable in the final report and show sensitivity analysis.

[09:38] Jonah (Redwood): ops question — do you expect to run the pilot against production traffic or synthetic?
[09:43] Alex (Veridian): prefer synthetic for now, but with a small canary (1% traffic) if initial pass looks good.

[09:50] Lena (Redwood): runner supports both; we recommend synthetic plus a low-volume production replay if compliance allows.

[09:58] Priya (Veridian): on BYOK, how is key management integrated in practice? we cannot have keys leave our KMS.
[10:04] Mark (Redwood): Redwood can integrate with your cloud KMS via a key-wrapping approach or use HSM-backed keys in a dedicated deployment. we'll detail both in the security deep dive.

[10:17] Sanjay (Veridian): are there specific format checks you perform for structured outputs?
[10:20] Lena (Redwood): yes — JSON schema validation, field-level type checks, numeric ranges and regex constraints. for nested arrays we check element-level schemas too. failures are categorized as critical (malformed JSON) vs minor (extra fields).

[10:36] Maya (Veridian): can Redwood produce diffs between model versions for each golden prompt? that would help triage.
[10:41] Jonah (Redwood): yes — our report includes per-case diffs and highlights new hallucinations or format regressions across versions.

[10:50] Sanjay (Veridian): metrics dashboard access — will Veridian engineers get read-only access?
[10:53] Mark (Redwood): yes read-only dashboards for engineers, with options to export raw logs.

[11:00] Maya (Veridian): what's your human reviewer flow? remote? can Veridian use internal SMEs?
[11:05] Lena (Redwood): Veridian SMEs preferred. we'll provide a small review app where reviewers can rate outputs and add comments. Redwood can coordinate a review panel if you need.

[11:16] Alex (Veridian): what about concurrency limits on the pilot? we need capacity for parallel batch jobs from our pipeline.
[11:22] Lena (Redwood): we'll include concurrency settings in the config; the dedicated pool can be sized to handle parallel steady-state plus bursts. we'll capture concurrency metrics in the benchmark.

[11:35] Sanjay (Veridian): question on data residency — some datasets must remain in EU. is that a blocker?
[11:40] Mark (Redwood): Redwood has region controls; we can run dedicated instances in EU region or in your VPC for data residency requirements. note this impacts latency for your US edge robots.

[11:52] Maya (Veridian): okay final check on acceptance gates and timeline — agreed?
[11:56] Sanjay (Veridian): yes i think so. let's confirm deliverables: golden prompts, regression set, traffic profile, security checklist.
[12:03] Mark (Redwood): i'll email a one-pager with the success criteria and timeline, plus links to the CSV templates and benchmark harness. Lena will share the harness repo. Jonah will propose pilot kick-off slots.

[12:15] Priya (Veridian): we'll review and schedule the security deep dive.

[12:20] Mark (Redwood): awesome, thanks all. any other questions?
[12:25] Maya (Veridian): none from me.
[12:27] Sanjay (Veridian): nope thanks everyone.
[12:30] Mark (Redwood): cool, meeting over.

Shared artifacts referenced:
- Pilot one-pager (link: https://redwood.co/share/VERIDIAN-POC-ONEPAGER)
- Benchmark harness repo (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-harness/tree/veridian)
- Golden prompt CSV template (link: https://redwood.co/share/golden-template.csv)
- Security packet (link: https://redwood.co/share/soc2-dpa.pdf)

Notes on measurement definitions (quick reference):
- Hallucination rate = (#cases flagged as hallucination) / (total evaluated cases) measured on combined auto+human sample
- Format pass rate = % cases that pass JSON schema and field checks
- Quality score = weighted composite (human, semantic, structure, hallucination penalty) - configurable
- Cost per 1k tokens = total infra + inference charges normalized by tokens generated

End of transcript.
